Tip: every room has its own brass plate. Turn the valves in the colours it lists, first to last.

gate_sign: THE DROWNED DYEWORKS. Larkin and Fennimore, partners in colour. Closed by flood. Closed by lawyers.

lines: A red wax seal, stamped with a Larkin rose. Someone pressed it into the mud on purpose.
You got a house seal.
A blue wax seal, stamped with a Fennimore bell. It floats. Fennimore things always float.
You got a house seal.
A red seal on a drying rack, holding nothing shut. The cloth it sealed was sold twice.
You got a house seal.
A blue seal at the bottom of a dye pit. It has been waiting for a diver, or a fool.
You got a house seal.
A seal that is half red and half blue. The only joint venture that ever worked.
You got a house seal.
A red seal stuck under a quay plank, next to a Larkin debt note. The note is newer.
You got a house seal.
A blue seal in the Madderby gutter. Blue water runs past it as if nothing happened.
You got a house seal.
A red seal tangled in the reeds by the pond. A rook has been using it as a mirror.
You got a house seal.
A blue seal wedged in the scree. Someone threw it as far from Madderby as they could.
You got a house seal.
A cracked seal in the moor, red under the blue. Paint over a feud and it shows through.
You got a house seal.
A rusty shift bell. You ring it. Somewhere below, a time card is stamped twenty years late.
The second shift bell. It rings flat, like a bell that has stopped believing in weekends.
The last shift bell. The sound runs up the stairs, looking for anyone who still works here.

shift_rung: The bell has been rung. Ringing it again would count as overtime.

lines: Hatch: Sluice Keeper Hatch, on shift. Twenty years on shift. Nobody rang the end-of-shift bells after the flood.
Hatch: Rules are rules. Ring all three bells down here and I can clock out. I don't remember where home is, but I'm told it has a chair.
Hatch: One in the vat hall, one up here in the lofts, one by the dye pits.
Hatch: Three bells. That's the end of my shift. Twenty years, no lunch break. I'll write a strongly worded letter.
Hatch: One thing before I go. If Aunt Prim sent you for the ledger: she sells everything twice. First to the one who pays, then to the one who'd pay more to see you robbed.
Hatch: Take these. They were for the flood. Turned out nobody needed reviving, only the payroll.

hatch_wait: Hatch: Three bells. Vat hall, lofts, dye pits. I'd do it myself, but I'm on shift.
sim: Sim: The Larkins pay me to find Fennimore things down here. The Fennimores pay me to lose them again.
sim_intro: Sim: Mudlark Sim. Everything that sinks is mine. You're sinking, so you're mine.
rufus: Rufus: Twenty years I've guarded this vat for the Larkins. It's empty. That's how good I am.
rufus_intro: Rufus: Larkin vat, Larkin rules. The rule is: you lose.
rufus_defeat: Rufus: Don't tell my aunt. She'll stop my pay. She stopped it in spring, but she'll stop it harder.
isolde: Isolde: Rufus and I have stood twelve steps apart for twenty years. We've never once talked. It's the healthiest relationship in Madderby.
isolde_intro: Isolde: Fennimore vat. If you're with the Larkins, you're drowning. If you're not, you're drowning politely.
isolde_defeat: Isolde: Blue never loses. It just takes longer to dry.
moll: Moll: I steal dye. Old dye, new dye, the dye off your boots. Business is grey this year.
moll_intro: Moll: Dye Thief Moll. Hand over your colours. All of them. Even the embarrassing ones.
moll_defeat: Moll: Keep your colours. They clash anyway.
agnes: Agnes: I dive the pits for lost rings. Found forty. Every one engraved 'to my only love'. Forty only loves. Madderby.
agnes_intro: Agnes: Pit Diver Agnes. Hold your breath. This takes a while.
agnes_defeat: Agnes: You'd make a good diver. You don't know when to give up either.
cardew_intro: Cardew: Cardew, loss adjuster. I've been adjusting this loss for twenty years. It's nearly adjusted.
Cardew: Both houses want this ledger. Both houses want me dead. So I sit on it. Literally. Shall we?
cardew_defeat: Cardew: Claim approved. Take the book. Page nine is the interesting one. Both signatures, one flood.
Cardew: The Larkins and the Fennimores opened the sluices together. Insurance paid. The workers didn't. Then each house told the town the other did it.
cardew: Cardew: Twenty years of feud, built on one afternoon of teamwork. Touching, really.

lines: The Dyeworks ledger. Page nine: 'Sluices opened at noon, by order of both houses. Wages: lost in the flood.'
A cold stove stands next to the desk. It looks hungry.
Cardew is sitting on the ledger. Literally. He won't stand up for anyone who hasn't beaten him.
An empty desk. Cardew is reading a novel now. He says it has a happier ending.
Ash in the stove. Twenty years of feud make a surprisingly small fire.
Prim: Aunt Prim. Everybody's aunt, nobody's relative. I fix things. Marriages, races, feuds.
Prim: The Larkins and the Fennimores have hated each other since the Dyeworks drowned. Bad for trade. Bad for my nerves.
Prim: There's a ledger in the counting room down there. Bring it to me and I'll make peace. You have my word. I have lots of words.
Prim: The way down is the sluice hatch at the end of the Stillwater jetty. Mind the damp. Damp is how this whole mess started.
Prim: Is that the ledger? Oh, you darling. Give it to Auntie.
Prim: Lovely. Peace is coming to Madderby. Run along now. Take the long way. Or don't. Your choice, darling.
prim_hand.action: set_flag ledger_to_prim; set_flag dye_ledger_done; betrayal prim_ledger

lines: Prim: The ledger, darling. Counting room, under Stillwater. Auntie is patient. Auntie is also counting.
Prim: You gave it to the widow. Sentimental. Sentiment is very bad for business, and worse for health.
Prim: You burned it. Twenty years of leverage, gone up a chimney. I'll send flowers. To your funeral, eventually.
Prim: Peace is lovely, isn't it? Both houses are paying me for it. Separately.

prim_caught: Hatch's warning sits in your ear. So you gave Prim the copy you drew by lamplight, every line perfect, page nine left blank.
By dusk the Larkins and the Fennimores both own a ledger that proves nothing, and both want a word with Aunt Prim.
You sell the real page nine to the harbour clerk. Anonymously. You're learning.
prim_struck: Prim sold the ledger to the Larkins at noon and to the Fennimores at one. At two she sold them your name as the thief.
For the first time in twenty years, a Larkin and a Fennimore walk side by side. Towards you.
ledger_prim: You fetched the Dyeworks ledger for Aunt Prim, the quay's fixer. She promised to end the dye feud.
She sold it to both houses and sold your name with it. Hatch and her own niece tried to warn you.
prim_ambush_lose: The two families split your coins exactly in half. It's the first fair deal they've made in twenty years.

lines: Wenna: You found the ledger. My Tobin ran the vat hall. His crew never got their last month's pay. The houses said the flood took it.
Wenna: Give it to me and both houses will pay what they owe. Every coin. I'll see to it personally.
Wenna: You found the ledger. Funny. My nephews say you've been beating them up for a bookie's coin.
Wenna: Give it to me anyway. I'm sure we can trust each other. We're both such honest people.

choices.action: set_flag ledger_to_wenna; set_flag dye_ledger_done; favor wenna_ledger

lines: Wenna: Twenty years I've watched the Larkins and the Fennimores spit at each other across my street. Neither of them ever looked at me.
Wenna: The houses are paying. Slowly, and through their teeth. It's the sweetest sound in Madderby.

wenna_betray: Wenna takes the ledger, kisses it, and walks straight down the hill to Aunt Prim's table on the quay.
Wenna: The houses owe me twenty years. You beat my boys for coin. I'm just collecting from everyone at once, love.
Two of her nephews are waiting at the bottom of the lane. They remember you.
wenna_reward: Wenna: Both houses paid within the week. Tobin's crew got their wages. With twenty years of interest. I insisted.
Wenna: This is from the crew. And this is from me. Don't tell the crew.
wenna_kept: Wenna: The houses are paying. Not quickly, not happily, but they're paying. Thank you, love.
ledger_wenna: You gave the Dyeworks ledger to Widow Wenna, whose husband's crew was never paid.
You had beaten her nephews for Bookie Lark's coin. She sold the ledger, and you, to Aunt Prim.
wenna_ambush_lose: The nephews take your coins and leave you a receipt signed 'with love, from the family you made'.

lines: Tansy: Tansy Hask. Aunt Prim's niece. She asked me to keep an eye on you. I've got two, so that's generous.
Tansy: Let's see if you're worth Auntie's coin.

tansy_1_defeat: Tansy: Hm. Auntie will want to know about this. Auntie wants to know about everything.

lines: Tansy: Fancy meeting you in a flooded basement. I'm here for the view. And for Auntie's ledger, if you drop it.
Tansy: Fine. You want a tip, from one of Auntie's tools to another? She sells everything twice. Ledgers, favours, nieces.
Tansy: I didn't tell you that. I don't tell anyone anything. It's a family value.
Tansy: So. The ledger's gone, the feud's still on and Auntie is smiling. That's never good for anyone.
Tansy: One last round. Then I'm leaving Corvane before she sells me to somebody with a boat.

tansy_3_defeat: Tansy: You're good. Too good. That makes you expensive, and expensive things get sold.
Tansy: Trust nobody on this quay. Start with me. I'm leaving anyway.
tansy_lose: Tansy: Auntie's going to love this story. She'll sell it by morning.

lines: Lark: Bookie Lark. I take bets on the dye feud. Larkins to win, Fennimores to win, both to lose. 'Both to lose' never pays out.
Lark: Until you. Three Larkin cousins and three Fennimore cousins are out on the roads, picking fights. Beat all six and 'both to lose' finally comes in.
Lark: I put my own money on it. You're my favourite tamer. Don't make me find a new favourite.
Lark: All six! Both to lose! Do you know how long I've waited to say that? Twenty years of other people's money.
Lark: Your share. And a word of advice: the cousins have a lot of aunts. Aunts talk.
lark_check.action: give_item power_brew 1; give_item strong_tonic 2; trust wenna 0 25

lines: Lark: Three red cousins, three blue cousins. On the quay, at Stillwater and up in Greyreach. Go make me rich.
Lark: The feud is back on, of course. Bad for Madderby. Wonderful for odds.

cousin_1: Ginny: Larkin red runs in my blood. Also in my sleeves. The vats leak.
cousin_1_intro: Ginny: Red, red, red! Fight me!
cousin_1_defeat: Ginny: That's going in the family grudge book. Page four hundred.
cousin_2: Bertram: I'm the Fennimore who reads. It means I know exactly why we hate the Larkins. Nobody else remembers.
cousin_2_intro: Bertram: For the bell and the blue! Or whatever the motto is this week.
cousin_2_defeat: Bertram: I'll write a pamphlet about this. Nobody will read it either.
cousin_3: Perpetua: Grandmother Larkin says Fennimores sink. I tested it. They float. I'm not allowed to talk about it.
cousin_3_intro: Perpetua: You look neutral. Neutral people are the worst. Battle!
cousin_3_defeat: Perpetua: Don't tell Grandmother. She'll disinherit me again.
cousin_4: Osric: I was born the day the Dyeworks flooded. Mother says I'm the only good thing that came out of it. Father says nothing came out of it.
cousin_4_intro: Osric: Blue blood! Literally! The dye never washes out!
cousin_4_defeat: Osric: Fine. I'll go back to being the family disappointment. It's a steady job.
cousin_5: Mungo: The Larkins sent me up here to keep watch on the Fennimores. There are no Fennimores up here. That's how well I watch.
cousin_5_intro: Mungo: Finally, somebody to fight! I was about to fight a rock.
cousin_5_defeat: Mungo: The rock would've been easier.
cousin_6: Clementine: I'm engaged to a Larkin. Nobody knows. If you tell anyone, I'll deny it and then marry him anyway.
cousin_6_intro: Clementine: I have to keep up appearances. Battle me like you mean it.
cousin_6_defeat: Clementine: Perfect. Everyone will think I really hate you. Thank you.

lines: Odo: Sealwright Odo. I made the wax seals for both dye houses. Red for the Larkins, blue for the Fennimores, same wax, same price, same pot.
Odo: After the flood they threw them all away, so nobody could prove they'd ever worked together. Ten are still out there. Bring them back to me.
Odo: Five sank into the Dyeworks. The rest are on the quay, in Madderby, here by the pond, up in Greyreach and out in the Woadfen.
Odo: All ten. Red and blue, side by side on my table. Exactly how they sat on every contract the houses ever signed together.
Odo: I'll melt them into one. Purple. The colour of a secret nobody can sell anymore. Here, for your trouble.
Odo: Ten seals. Five in the Dyeworks, five out in Corvane. Wax lasts longer than loyalty.
Odo: One purple seal. I keep it on my desk. It frightens the right people.
